hero.headline_b: I build applications from the server all the way to the screen people use.
hero.intro: Software engineer with an Informatics degree from Universitas Budi Luhur. Day to day I write backends in Golang and NestJS and frontends in Next.js. 18 projects so far, some of them live and used by clients.
hero.skills_hint: The technical term on the left, what it means on the right.

skills.title: Backends split into separate services
skills.desc: One big app is split into small services that talk through Kafka and gRPC. If one part is busy, the rest keeps working.

skills.title: Code that stays tidy and safe to change
skills.desc: Business logic is kept apart from the database and framework, so new features don't mean tearing up what already works. Checked with Jest unit tests.

skills.title: Websites that load fast and show up on Google
skills.desc: Pages open quickly on phones, look right in search results, and business owners can edit the content themselves without a developer.
skills.note: live and used by the client

skills.title: Features that update without refreshing
skills.desc: The server runs on Cloudflare, close to users. Guest photos appear in the event gallery the moment they're uploaded.

hero.featured_desc: From the outside it looks like any online store. The difference is inside: the system is split into 7 independent Go services, so it keeps running under load and each part can grow on its own.
hero.featured_stack: Golang · PostgreSQL · Next.js · React + Vite · Docker · VPS

featured_points.desc: One front door for every request: load is spread evenly and access is checked before it reaches a service.
Each part of the store has its own database plus a copy. One fails, the rest keep going and data stays safe.
Services send each other updates without waiting on one another.
Services call each other directly and fast.
Order status changes on the shopper's screen without refreshing.
Every request can be traced and system health shows up on dashboards.
Emails get tested before they reach real users.
Each service has its own repo and is tested and shipped automatically with GitHub Actions.

about.label: About me
about.title: I started with computer networks. Now I build web apps from the server to the screen.
paragraphs: In vocational school I studied Computer and Network Engineering: setting up LANs, configuring Debian servers, and troubleshooting Cisco gear. That taught me to think about what happens behind the scenes, not just what shows up on screen.

After earning my Informatics degree at Universitas Budi Luhur, I focused on web development. I now work as a Frontend Web Developer at Zegen Solusi Mandiri on BTN's Rumah Murah / Bale Lelang project, building Single Sign-On, the admin panel, and public pages.
Outside work, I build websites for clients and I'm building Jajanim to go deeper into backend work: microservices, event-driven design, and deploying to my own VPS.
